name: fig_access_constraint.png
caption: (a) Corpus funnel for the six registered diseases: papers in the title/abstract corpus, with open full text (share of the corpus in brackets), eligible after full-text screening and extracted. HA20, the development disease, kept its pilot corpus and was not full-text screened. Open full text ranges from 13.7% (Tangier) to 53.1% (HA20) of the corpus; every eligible paper was extracted. (b) OMIM allelic variants recovered anywhere in the run (tiers 1+2), with Wilson 95% confidence intervals: 43 of 75 pooled (57.3%, 46.1-67.9), ranging from 2 of 19 (10.5%) for Tangier to 8 of 9 (88.9%) for HA20. Below, where OMIM's 84 source papers for these variants sit: 5 were extracted, 38 are in the corpus without an open copy, 38 were never returned by the searches and 3 were not in the corpus (screened unclear/other). Where the source paper was extracted, 8 of 14 allelic variants were recovered from it: literature coverage, not reading, is the binding constraint.

name: fig_gatekeeper_by_run.png
caption: Gatekeeper shares per main run: the share of model claims that a second model read (gatekeeper v4) judged (a) unsupported or with its span not found and (b) not fully supported (unsupported plus partially supported), with exact 95% confidence intervals where available; numbers at right are model claims judged. Runs are grouped by standing: the registered six on the frozen pipeline (HA20 is the development disease), with the five confirmatory diseases and all six pooled (diamonds); the extension five (D-52), whose not-fully-supported shares are shown without intervals (open circles); and the exploratory Majeed run. Addendum batches are not shown. Unsupported shares range from 0.20% (HA20, 46/23,129) to 0.86% (ATS, 54/6,268); the five confirmatory registered diseases pooled give 0.43% (248/57,819; 0.38–0.49) and all six 0.36% (294/80,948; 0.32–0.41). These shares are a model reading of model output, not an error rate: no human audit of these runs has been returned, and in the pilot people found about 6% of claims unsupported where the gatekeeper found 0.04–0.3%, so no accuracy claim and no comparison with the 2% target can be made from this figure.

name: fig_human_assessment.png
caption: Design of the human assessment (D-55); the diagram shows the procedure only, not results. Stage 1 (calibration, due 2026-11-22): the PI labelled 99 candidate claims from the registered runs, blind to the gatekeeper's verdicts; a set rule fixed before any label existed, with two recorded amendments, selected 40 claims (20 unsupported, 20 supported by his label, from 39 papers). Nine raters (R1 to R9) rate the same 40 claims, each in their own order, without seeing reference labels, gatekeeper verdicts or source pools. A rater qualifies as a registered rater by catching at least 15 of the 20 unsupported claims and passing at least 18 of the 20 supported ones. After calibration the PI decides who goes on and whether to run Plan A (registered six: 250 audit claims, 50 ClinVar misses, 214 gap candidates) or Plan B (all twelve: 527, 146 and 269); these are planning figures, not measurements. Stage 2: (a) each audit claim is read by 3 raters in rotating, overlapping groups of three (84 groups with nine raters), with a registered pair and a tie-breaker named per claim and the pre-registered rule C (at most 4 of 250 unsupported) unchanged; (b) each ClinVar miss is triaged by 2 raters, with the PI settling differences; (c) each gap candidate is adjudicated by 2 raters, with a third where they differ on the decision or across the pathogenic / uncertain line. No submission record is prepared without panel approval and the PI's sign-off; nothing has been submitted.

name: fig_o2_concordance.png
caption: ClinVar concordance (O2) per disease for three measures: HGVS recall at tier 1 (same GRCh38 allele), HGVS recall at tiers 1+2 (adding same-protein matches for papers with no cDNA), and tier-1 overlap, the share of extracted alleles present in ClinVar (not precision). Dots are percentages, lines Wilson 95% intervals as reported in the experimental log, and n/N is shown at the right of each panel. Rows are the registered six (run 2026-10-20; ClinVar release 2026-10-12, snapshot 2026-10-19), the extension five (D-52; snapshot 2026-11-14, ClinVar variant_summary of 09 Nov 2026) and Majeed syndrome (exploratory; snapshot 2026-11-15, same ClinVar release); the groups use different snapshots and are shown beside each other, not pooled. * Danon figures predate the D-43 re-normalization, which moved one placed Danon variant and unplaced another; O2 was not re-run. † Blau uses the D-53 NOD2 legacy-transcript fallback; under the registered rule its tier-1 recall was 4.5% (1/22), and 17 of its 19 remaining misses come from papers that give only protein changes in legacy numbering. Tier-1 recall in the registered six is low (10.1% to 35.0%) and the misses are concentrated in single papers. Majeed's recall (6.6%, 5/76) is low mainly because ClinVar cites some corpus papers for variants those papers do not report. Many denominators are small and the intervals wide. No threshold applies to O2 (D-03).

name: fig_pipeline_overview.png
caption: GP-RareLink pipeline and its database-held-out evaluation. Top lane: the extraction pipeline, frozen with pre-registration v1.0 on 2026-10-20. Open-access case reports found by PubMed and backward citation search and screened by Claude Sonnet helpers are read one paper per Claude Opus helper; every extracted value carries a verbatim quote and the PMID, and phenotypes are observed, excluded or not reported. A deterministic span check confirms each quote occurs verbatim in its paper (241,730 values, 0 problems, registered six diseases), a second Claude read (gatekeeper v4) keeps only claims it judges supported, and Stage 4 merges people only on explicit one-to-one citations, normalizes variants with VariantValidator on MANE Select while keeping the original string, binds HPO and Mondo terms and writes schema-validated GA4GH Phenopackets v2. An automated isolation test keeps ClinVar and OMIM out of extraction. Bottom lane: the harness reads a dated ClinVar snapshot and the OMIM entry pages frozen on 2026-10-28 only after extraction, to score concordance (O2) and list gap candidates absent from both databases (O3), for which evidence dossiers of verbatim quotes propose no classification. People then audit gatekeeper-supported claims (O1), triage ClinVar misses and adjudicate gap candidates; the gatekeeper's verdicts are a model reading, not an error rate, which only the human audit measures.
